REPORT: /tmp/findings/cli-flags.md
Artifacts: /tmp/probe/cli-flags/runs/<label>/{out,err,exit}; pristine usage = /tmp/probe/cli-flags/runs/h/err (2487B, md5 6c8134f10bf0803d9831cfa3540d7b86); trailing-space-marked copy = /tmp/probe/cli-flags/usage_marked.txt

TOP FINDINGS

1. `-` reads STDIN (undocumented). Only when it is the SOLE resolved target (positional or via -file-path). Path token becomes `<standard-input>`; output ALWAYS to stdout; no file written; `-output` is not even validated (`-output bad -` exits 0). `- a.go`, `a.go -`, `- -`, `- -format` all treat `-` as a literal filename.
2. Stdin hint `reading from stdin, press Ctrl+D when done...\n` (stderr, NO log timestamp) printed only when stdin is a char device (/dev/null, pty) or Stat() fails (closed fd). NOT for pipes, FIFOs, regular files. Printed BEFORE the `Paths:` line and before -imports-order validation.
3. Deprecated flags make a SUCCESSFUL run exit 1. `-file-path a.go` formats the file, then logs the deprecation notice and `All changes to file are applied, but command-line syntax should be fixed` → exit 1. Same for `-local`. Warnings come AFTER all processing; -file-path notice before -local.
4. `-file-path` is still a real target source, APPENDED AFTER positionals: `-file-path b.go a.go` → `Paths: [a.go b.go]`.
5. Empty-string values for `-file-path`/`-local`/`-project-name` are treated as UNSET (no warning, no target, no go.mod bypass).
6. Version flags short-circuit EVERYTHING after flag.Parse: no go.mod needed, no path/output/imports-order validation, no logs. Both go to STDOUT, exit 0. `-version-only` (34B `3.0.0-...\n`) BEATS `-version` (164B block) in either order. `-h` still beats `-version`.
7. `Usage of %s:` uses os.Args[0] VERBATIM as invoked (`./gir`, `gir`, `/abs/path`) — do not hardcode.
8. Usage body is stdlib flag.PrintDefaults: lexicographic, `"  -"+name` (+` string`), then `\n` + 4 spaces + TAB, with every embedded `\n` in the usage string → `\n    \t`. Exactly 4 lines carry a trailing space (the first four -imports-order lines).
9. README is STALE vs binary: `-separate-named` = "Option will separate named imports from the rest of the imports, per group. Optional parameter."; `-version` = "Show version information"; `-version-only` exists but is undocumented. 18 flags total.
10. Validation ORDER (pinned): flag.Parse → version-only → version → merge paths → empty check (usage+fatal) → stdin resolution → imports-order parse (usage+fatal, BEFORE the `Paths:` log) → log `Paths:` → per target: log `Processing`, project name (usage+fatal), `-output` validation INSIDE processing (after `Processing`, NO usage) → deprecation epilogue → -set-exit-status.
11. flag.Usage() is called on SOME fatal paths only: yes for no-targets, `unknown order group type`, `Could not determine project name`; NO for `invalid output`, `Failed to fix file`. Usage lands BETWEEN the `Processing` line and the fatal line.
12. `Paths: %v` is Go's `[]string` `%v`: `[a.go b.go c.go]` — spaces, no quotes/commas. Duplicates NOT deduped (processed and logged once per occurrence). Empty-string target → `Paths: []` and `Processing ` (trailing space) then `path is not set`.
13. `Processing X` is per COMMAND-LINE TARGET, not per file: recursive run over 3 files logs one `Processing .`. Still logged for targets excluded by `-excludes` (exit 0).
14. Flags AFTER the first positional become targets (Go stops parsing): `a.go -output stdout` → `Paths: [a.go -output stdout]`, a.go IS rewritten, then exit 1 on `-output`. Lone `--` is consumed correctly.
15. Exit codes: 0 = success, -h/--help/-help, version flags, `-list-diff` alone (even when files differ). 1 = no args, bad -output, bad -imports-order, missing/unparseable target, missing go.mod, any deprecated flag, -set-exit-status with a change. 2 = unknown flag, `flag needs an argument: -X`, `invalid boolean value "x" for -format: parse error`.
16. Timestamps are `YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM:SS ` with SLASHES (od -c verified; terminals here render dashes).
17. No subcommands: `version`/`help` as bare words are treated as file targets.
18. `-project-name X` fully bypasses the go.mod lookup (exit 0 in a dir with no go.mod).
19. `-list-diff` prints ABSOLUTE paths to stdout, never writes the file, exits 0; pair with -set-exit-status for exit 1.
20. `-output stdout` with 2 files concatenates formatted output with NO separator/header. Plain runs are idempotent (identical md5 after 2nd run).

Report: `/tmp/findings/separate-named.md` (1102 lines). Scratch: `/tmp/probe/separate-named/`

DIMENSION: -separate-named

CORE RULE
- "Named" == the ImportSpec has a Name node. `_` and `.` BOTH count as named. An alias equal to the package's own name (`fmt "fmt"`, `slices "golang.org/x/exp/slices"`) also counts — no alias-vs-package-name comparison is done.
- Applied per group, to every group (std, general, company, project) independently.
- Within a group: unnamed block first, then ONE completely empty line (`\n\n\t`, no whitespace), then the named block.
- Sorting is unchanged by the flag: whole group sorted by tuple (path, alias) byte-wise ascending; unnamed (alias "") sorts before any alias for the same path. The flag only stable-partitions that sorted list. So the named sub-block is sorted BY PATH, not by alias.
- Byte order confirmed: '.'(0x2E) < 'B' < 'Z' < '_'(0x5F) < 'a'. No case folding.
- Empty sub-blocks emit nothing ⇒ never two adjacent blank lines, never a blank right after `import (` or before `)`.

INTERACTIONS
- `blanked`/`dotted` groups in -imports-order are 100% named ⇒ flag is a no-op on them (no leading blank). If only `blanked` is in the order, dot imports stay in std/general and DO get pushed into those groups' named blocks (and vice versa).
- -set-alias runs BEFORE grouping ⇒ aliases the tool adds get separated. -set-alias never strips an existing alias.
- -rm-unused runs before separation; all of -rm-unused/-set-alias/-format/-separate-named compose.
- -set-exit-status correctly returns 1 when only the separation is missing; returns 0 on an already-separated file.
- Idempotent (verified md5 stable over 3 runs, both default and blanked/dotted orders).

TOP GOTCHAS
1. README's -separate-named example is WRONG. It shows `extpkg "google.com/golang/pkg"` before `extslice "github.com/PeterRK/slices"`. Binary emits extslice first (path sort). Everything else in that example matches byte-for-byte.
2. README's flag help text is wrong. Binary usage line is exactly:
   `  -separate-named` / `    <TAB>Option will separate named imports from the rest of the imports, per group. Optional parameter.`
3. Comment alignment changes: the inserted blank line breaks go/printer's alignment run, so trailing-comment padding is computed per sub-block. `"fmt" // c1` / `"os"  // c2` (2 cols) vs the un-separated `"fmt"              // c1` (aligned to `al "path/filepath"`). Reimplementation must insert the blank line into the source text before format.Source.
4. -use-cache silently defeats -separate-named: cache is keyed on file content only, not flags. Second run prints NOTHING to stdout even with `-output stdout`. Cache at `<os.UserCacheDir>/goimports-reviser/<32-hex>`.
5. Duplicate import paths are preserved (not deduped) and are split across the unnamed/named boundary.
6. Doc comments above import specs are dropped (flag-independent); trailing `//x cmt` is NOT re-spaced.

FLAG PARSING
- `-separate-named`, `=true`, `=1`, `--separate-named` all enable; `=false`/`=0` disable; `=yes` ⇒ usage to stderr, exit 2. `-separate-named true f.go` treats `true` as a target path ⇒ `Paths: [true f.go]`, `Failed to fix file: open <dir>/true: no such file or directory`, exit 1.

DEGENERATE
- `import ()` ⇒ output is exactly `package p\n`. `import "C"` in its own decl is left untouched; only the parenthesized block is reorganized. Separate single-import decls are merged into one block.

Report written. Returning the numbered gap list.

Report: /tmp/probe/cli-flags-critic/critique.md

**Spot-checks: 12 of the colleague's claims re-run, 0 found wrong.** (usage md5 `6c8134f10bf0803d9831cfa3540d7b86`/2487B; `-version` 164B; B7 version-only precedence; B13 empty target 2629B incl. `Processing ` trailing space; B18 three-paths + a.go rewritten first; B23 rows 3 & 4 incl. 121B/2539B sizes; B15 stdin-hint matrix; B20/B21 empty-value-as-unset; B30 133B concat; B12 non-.go message; `--` alone.) The report is not *wrong* — it is incomplete in ways that will break a reimplementation.

**Gaps, most important first:**

1. **`-output` is never validated or honored for DIRECTORY targets.** `-output bad .` → exit **0**, silent. `-output stdout -recursive .` → stdout **0 bytes** and the files are **rewritten in place** (md5 `ce36de79…`→`1c63906d…`). The report's `-output` rules only hold for file/stdin targets.
2. **`-set-exit-status` is a no-op for directory targets.** `-set-exit-status -recursive .` on a dirty tree → exit **0** despite rewriting both files. Control `-set-exit-status d1.go` → exit 1. Exception: `-list-diff -set-exit-status -recursive .` → exit **1**. The report's blanket "change needed → 1" row is wrong for dirs.
3. **`-list-diff` on a single FILE target lists it UNCONDITIONALLY**, even a verified fixpoint (`-output stdout clean1.go | cmp - clean1.go` identical, yet it is listed). Directory targets DO filter (only `dirty1.go`). The report implies uniform "lists differing files".
4. **Whole undocumented error message + validation rule for `-imports-order`:** `use default at least 4 parameters to sort groups of your imports: "std,general,company,project"` (usage block first, then TS line, stderr 2603B, exit 1). Real rule: **all four of std/general/company/project must be present**; `std,std,std,std` and `blanked,dotted,std,general` (4 tokens) both fail.
5. **Undocumented top-level error family:** `Failed to fix directory %s: failed to walk dif: failed to fix %s: %v` — `%s`=raw argv dir spelling, inner path absolute, and the literal typo **`dif`** (not `diff`) must be reproduced. Report lists only `Failed to fix file: %v`.
6. **go.mod resolution is far more subtle than "walks up".** It walks up from `filepath.Dir(target)`, so `cd sub/deep && tool x.go` **fails** (`open go.mod: no such file or directory`) while `cd sub/deep && tool $PWD/x.go` **succeeds**. Relative walks stop at `.`.
7. **cwd `go.mod` is a silent fallback:** target `/tmp/nogomodroot/d/x.go` (no go.mod up-tree) → exit **0** when cwd has a `go.mod`, exit 1 when it doesn't. The fallback is a literal `open("go.mod")` in cwd with **no** upward walk — which also explains why the error text is always bare `go.mod`, never `/go.mod`.
8. **Stdin resolves the project from cwd UPWARD** (absolute), unlike relative file targets: `cd up/sub/deep && tool - < in.go` → exit 0, while `tool x.go` in the same cwd → exit 1.
9. **`-output write` (report's open question #1): resolved.** `write` == `file` for plain runs; `-list-diff -output write x.go` → exit 0, lists the abs path **and** rewrites the file.
10. `-imports-order` token handling unspecified in the report: tokens are **space-trimmed before validation** (`std, general` → count error, not `unknown … " general"`); **empty string == unset** (exit 0); validation runs **before** the count check (`,std` → `unknown order group type: ""`); **first** bad token is reported (`bad1,bad2` → `"bad1"`).
11. `-output` value set is exactly `{file,write,stdout}`, **case-sensitive, no trimming**, and `""` is **not** unset (`invalid output "" specified`) — unlike `-file-path`/`-local`/`-project-name`/`-imports-order`.
12. **stdin + `-list-diff`** prints `<standard-input>\n` and **suppresses the formatted code** entirely (exit 0). Not covered.
13. File-vs-directory branch selection: chosen by stat-is-dir, not spelling. Nonexistent dirs (`nopedir`, `nopedir/`) take the **file** branch (`Failed to fix file: open …`).
14. Report's pseudocode says `log.Fatalf("…: %+v", err)` for the project-name error but the strings section says `%v` — unresolved inconsistency for a byte-exact reimplementation.
15. `-recursive` on a file target and on an empty dir are silent no-ops (exit 0, Paths/Processing only) — never stated.
16. Repeated flags: stdlib last-wins (`-output bad -output stdout a.go` → exit 0). Not covered.
17. `-list-diff -output write -set-exit-status` idempotency: exit 1 then exit 0, path listed both times.
18. Unprobed and needed: directory walk order for >2 files; whether `vendor/`, `testdata/`, dot-dirs are descended; whether a non-recursive run can fail on a subdirectory's broken file.
19. Unprobed: `-excludes` pattern grammar (only exact name, comma list, `*.go` tested — all suppressed the error); whether it is anchored, glob or prefix, and `dir/` vs `dir`.
20. Unprobed: whether the directory branch honors `-project-name`, `-company-prefixes`, `-separate-named` the same way as the file branch.
21. Unprobed: reachability of any exit code other than 0/1/2, and whether `-use-cache` perturbs any CLI-visible output.
